travelAdvisory.summary:
Exercise increased cautionin Egypt due to terrorism, crime, and health. Some areas have increased risk. 

The U.S. Embassy has limited ability to help dual national U.S.-Egyptian citizens who are arrested or detained.
Egyptian law considers dual citizens to be solely Egyptian citizens.

healthcare.summary: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Egypt. Emergency numbers (122/123/180), pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccination requirements, water safety, and travel insurance advice.

medications.prescriptionRules: A prescription is required for prescription medications but enforcement varies. Antibiotics and many drugs available OTC. Carry all medications in original packaging with a doctor's note in English.

restrictedMeds.name: ADHD stimulant medications (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Stimulants are controlled substances. Bring original prescription, doctor's letter, and only the amount needed. Declare at customs. A permit from the Egyptian Ministry of Health may be required.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine is controlled. Many codeine products are restricted. Carry alternatives if possible.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications (diazepam, alprazolam, etc.)
restrictedMeds.note: Benzodiazepines require documentation. Carry a doctor's letter explaining medical necessity.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotics (morphine, tramadol, etc.)
restrictedMeds.note: Strong narcotics require strict documentation and potentially a permit from Egyptian authorities.

medications.bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications with generic names in English. Keep medications in original packaging. For controlled substances, carry original prescriptions and a note explaining medical necessity. Check with the Egyptian consulate about import permits for controlled medications.

connectivity.simOptions: Vodafone Egypt, Orange, or Etisalat prepaid SIMs at airport arrivals hall. Need passport. Data plans very cheap — ~50 EGP for 10GB.
connectivity.wifiAvailability: Free WiFi at most hotels and many cafes in Cairo and tourist areas. Quality can be unreliable. Limited in Upper Egypt and desert areas.
connectivity.bestOption: Vodafone Egypt prepaid SIM at Cairo airport — counters open 24/7. Best coverage nationwide. eSIM via Airalo as alternative.

cultural.tipping: Expected everywhere. 10-15% at restaurants. Tip guides, drivers, hotel staff. Baksheesh (small tips) is part of daily life — carry small bills.
cultural.dressCode: Modest dress, especially for women. Cover shoulders and knees, particularly at mosques. Women should bring a headscarf for mosque visits. Men should wear long pants at religious sites.
cultural.greetings: Handshake common between same gender. Men should wait for a woman to extend her hand first. 'As-salamu alaykum' (peace be upon you) is the standard greeting.
taboos: Using left hand to eat or pass items
Showing the soles of your feet
Photography of military installations or government buildings
Drinking alcohol in public during Ramadan
cultural.haggling: Expected and essential at bazaars, markets, and with taxi drivers. Start at 25-40% of asking price. Take your time — haggling is a social ritual.

practical.visaFreeCountries: US citizens: visa on arrival (USD $25) or e-Visa. UK, EU also eligible for visa on arrival. Single entry, 30 days.
practical.bestTimeToVisit: October-April (cooler). December-February most pleasant. Avoid June-August (extreme heat 40°C+). Ramadan dates vary — plan accordingly.

stalenessWarnings.message: Some data in this profile may be outdated. Connect to the internet to refresh.

steps: File a police report immediately — get the report number, you will need it
Contact the US Embassy or nearest consulate: Contact the nearest US Embassy
Bring the police report + any ID you have (driver's license, copy of passport)
Apply for an Emergency Passport (usually issued within 1-2 business days)
Notify your travel insurance and airline of the situation
stolenPassport.notes: Keep a digital copy of your passport in cloud storage (Google Photos, iCloud) and email yourself a scan before travel.

steps: Go to the nearest police station (or call 122)
Bring ID or a copy of your passport if available
Request a written report — ask for an English copy or certified translation if needed
Keep the report number safe — required for insurance claims
For theft: list all stolen items with approximate values
policeReport.notes: In many countries, tourist police stations are available in major cities — they have English-speaking staff. Ask your hotel concierge for the nearest tourist police.

steps: If involved in an accident: do not move vehicles if anyone is injured
Call police (122) and ambulance (123) if there are injuries
Exchange contact, license, and insurance details with other parties
Document the scene with photos before moving vehicles
Contact your rental car company's emergency line
Contact your travel insurance's 24h assistance line
roadsideAssistance.notes: Traffic drives on the RIGHT. An International Driving Permit (IDP) is recommended for most foreign licenses. Rental vehicles are available at major airports and cities.

immediate: Drink 3-4 liters of water per day
Wear loose, light-colored clothing and sun protection
Avoid prolonged exposure when temperatures exceed 40°C
after: Seek medical care for signs of heat stroke: hot dry skin, confusion
